items.title: Fixed-boundary anyonic fusion-path space
items.statement_or_definition: For a complex fusion category, a simple site label a, simple boundary labels b,c, and n≥0, fix the left-associated object T_n=(((b⊗a)⊗a)…⊗a) and define H_(a,n;b,c)=Hom(c,T_n). A path is x_0=b,…,x_n=c with a retained basis index in Hom(x_j,x_(j−1)⊗a) at every vertex; no multiplicity index is suppressed.
items.strategy: Define the typed Hom space, parenthesization, split-space bases, and path labels before constructing operators.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; only finite-dimensional spaces and finite simple-object sets are used.

items.title: Tensor-invertible objects, fusion-ring units, and invertible operators
items.statement_or_definition: Define tensor-invertibility of an object by a two-sided tensor inverse, a fusion-ring unit by an inverse in K_0(C) with integral coefficients, and operator invertibility only relative to a specified vector space and linear map with a two-sided inverse.
items.strategy: Separate the three domains and state the inverse required in each one.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; only finite direct-sum multiplicities are used.

items.title: Fusion paths give a basis of the fixed-boundary path space
items.statement_or_definition: The path composites indexed by every admissible simple-label sequence and every split-space basis index form a basis of Hom(c,b⊗a^⊗n). Its dimension is the sum over paths of the product of the vertex fusion multiplicities.
items.strategy: Induct on n using the finite semisimple decomposition of T_(n−1)⊗a into simple summands, retaining each inclusion multiplicity.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; basis selections are finite-dimensional and finite at each fixed n.

items.title: Unitary fusion paths form an orthonormal Hilbert basis
items.statement_or_definition: If the fusion category is unitary and every split-space basis is orthonormal, the path composites form an orthonormal basis of H_(a,n;b,c) under the Hom-space inner product induced by the dagger.
items.strategy: Use orthogonal simple decompositions at each fusion vertex and inductively tensor the isometric inclusions.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; the proof uses only finite orthogonal direct sums.

items.title: Frobenius–Schur sign in a normalized anyonic vacuum channel
items.statement_or_definition: For a self-dual simple a with a one-dimensional vacuum channel, a supplied normalized self-duality datum has coev=√d_a v and ev=κ_a√d_a v† with κ_a∈{+1,−1}; define κ_a as the FS sign in this explicit cup/cap convention. The item does not assert such a datum exists for every category.
items.strategy: Specify the pivotal/cup/cap normalization and the coefficient convention used by the local F-symbol.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all duality spaces involved are one-dimensional.

items.title: Local anyonic channel projector
items.statement_or_definition: For adjacent copies of a simple site charge a and an allowed fusion output s, let Π_s be the projection onto the s-channel in the tree where this pair is fused first. If F_i is the typed associator change from the fixed path tree to that pair-first tree, define P_(i,s)=F_i^−1 Π_s F_i. In the unitary case, use orthonormal multiplicity bases and interpret Π_s as the orthogonal channel projection.
items.strategy: Fix source/target parenthesizations and the row/column convention of the supplied F-move before defining conjugation.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all decompositions and multiplicity spaces are finite.

items.title: Vacuum F-coefficient records the Frobenius–Schur sign
items.statement_or_definition: In the specified self-dual vacuum normalization, (F_(aaa)^a)_(1,1)=κ_a/d_a, and consequently δ_a:=1/((F_(aaa)^a)^−1)_(1,1)=κ_a d_a.
items.strategy: Write the two vacuum-channel tree vectors as normalized cup insertions, identify their overlap as the F-entry, and apply the typed snake identity.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; the proof is a one-dimensional cap/cup calculation.

items.title: The Fibonacci ring class is a unit but its simple object is not tensor-invertible
items.statement_or_definition: In the coherent Fibonacci category with simple labels 1,τ and τ²=1+τ, [τ] is a unit in K_0(C) with inverse [τ]−[1], but τ has no tensor-inverse object because every object class has nonnegative integral coefficients.
items.strategy: Compute the ring inverse, then compare its signed coefficients with the nonnegative simple-object decomposition of any candidate inverse object.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; finite semisimple objects are finite direct sums of simple objects.

items.title: Canonical F-move paths give the same channel operator
items.statement_or_definition: For fixed ordered input charges and fixed source/target parenthesizations, any two sequences of associator F-moves inducing the same canonical rebracketing give the same coordinate map and hence the same conjugated local channel projector.
items.strategy: Identify each F-move sequence with a canonical associator composite and apply Mac Lane coherence in canonical-map form.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; only finite compositions of associators are compared.

items.title: Local channel projections are orthogonal idempotents
items.statement_or_definition: For each fixed adjacent pair, the family (P_(i,s))_s consists of pairwise orthogonal self-adjoint idempotents and sums to the identity on the path space.
items.strategy: Conjugate the orthogonal direct-sum channel projections by the unitary F-move and multiply the resulting matrices.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; only finite-dimensional unitary matrices are used.

items.title: Vacuum-channel anyonic projectors satisfy Temperley–Lieb relations
items.statement_or_definition: For identical self-dual simple sites a with one-dimensional vacuum fusion and the normalized FS sign κ_a, define U_i=δ_aP_(i,1) with δ_a=κ_ad_a. Then U_i²=δ_aU_i, U_iU_(i+1)U_i=U_i, and U_iU_j=U_jU_i for |i−j|>1.
items.strategy: Compute the adjacent triple block from the vacuum F-entry and use tensor functoriality for distant pairs.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all operators act on finite-dimensional fusion-path spaces.

items.title: A multiplicity-two fusion vertex contributes two path states
items.statement_or_definition: Given a finite semisimple fusion category and a simple vertex with N_(x,a)^y=2, fix a basis of Hom(y,x⊗a). A fixed surrounding path through this vertex contributes exactly two linearly independent basis states, indexed by μ=1,2; deleting μ collapses a two-dimensional path summand to one coordinate and is not a basis.
items.strategy: Apply the path-basis theorem to the two basis inclusions at the specified vertex and compare dimensions.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; only one finite two-dimensional multiplicity space is selected.

items.title: Ising periodic paths split into two spin-chain sectors
items.statement_or_definition: Assume a coherent unitary Ising fusion category with labels 1,η,D and the usual fusion rules, and the displayed three-D/total-D F/R block. For a closed periodic D-reference path of length L≥1, the path space is zero for odd L and for L=2N with N≥1 is a direct sum of two 2^N-dimensional tensor-product sectors. The one-step cyclic shift gives an explicit basis bijection between sectors; it does not identify their operators with a single-lattice noninvertible translation operator.
items.strategy: Use only the fusion-rule transition graph for the path count, then give the two sector-to-bit maps and check the stated F/R block separately.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all path sets are finite. The category-coherence hypothesis is explicit and is not proved by the sector F/R calculation.

items.title: Fibonacci path projectors and categorical noninvertibility
items.statement_or_definition: In the coherent Fibonacci category, the three-τ total-τ path space has two channels, its vacuum-channel projectors have explicit 2×2 matrices with FS sign +1 and loop δ=φ, and [τ] is a ring unit although τ is not tensor-invertible. The identity operator on this space is invertible; this is a separate operator-level fact.
items.strategy: Use the supplied coherent F/R data, compute the two channel projections in the tree basis, and prove the ring/object/operator distinctions directly.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle; all spaces and sums are finite-dimensional.

items.statement:
Use the coherent Fibonacci category and pullback-R convention of [[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]]. Write $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, $u=\phi^{-1}$, and $v=\phi^{-1/2}$. The simple fusion rule is $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$. For three tensor inputs $\tau,\tau,\tau$, comprising the incoming boundary $b=\tau$ and two sites ($n=2$), with output $c=\tau$, the path space $H_{\tau,2;\tau,\tau}$ has ordered basis $(\mathbf1,\tau)$ according to the intermediate charge. The supplied associator block is

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix}.$$

On these three tensor inputs the two adjacent vacuum-channel projectors are $P_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ and $P_2=F^{-1}P_1F$; the first pair includes the incoming boundary charge. For the literal three-site problem $n=3$, still with $b=c=\tau$, the four tensor inputs give a three-dimensional space with path basis $(x_1,x_2)=(\mathbf1,\tau),(\tau,\mathbf1),(\tau,\tau)$. The two adjacent pairs among the three sites have projectors

$$Q_1=\begin{pmatrix}u^2&0&uv\\0&0&0\\uv&0&v^2\end{pmatrix},\qquad Q_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&u^2&uv\\0&uv&v^2\end{pmatrix}.$$

Both are rank-one orthogonal projections and $Q_1Q_2Q_1=\phi^{-2}Q_1$; hence $\phi Q_i$ obey the adjacent Temperley–Lieb relation. Thus the two-site $2\times2$ block and the three-site $3\times3$ problem are both retained with their correct domains. The object $\tau$ is not tensor-invertible even though its fusion-ring class is a unit. The identity on this two-dimensional path space is an invertible operator; the local rank-one channel projection is not.
proof_obligations: Retain the two-site/two-dimensional block and prove the literal three-site/three-dimensional fixed-boundary Fibonacci projectors, with exact F-moves and signed TL relations.
